Service Requirements The Contractor must provide printing services, including the following tasks: • Graphic design and creation of annual report content for various Embassy offices. • Graphic design and creation of brochures, information portfolios, folders, advertising publications, flyers, and similar materials for the Embassy's promotional events. • Printing and/or photocopying of documents, brochures, and portfolios in a professional manner, ensuring clear colors, photographs, text, and images for finished products. Preference will be given to contractors offering multiple printing methods, such as commercial, digital, press, and web-based printing. • Supplying stock images for publications, as needed. • Providing printing designs for requesting offices to review and confirm prior to production. The Contractor is responsible for installing, setting up, and delivering printed items to U.S. Embassy Hanoi events. • Material Requirements: The Contractor shall present several material options for the Embassy's selection prior to submitting a quote. Services must include all necessary supplies — such as equipment, toner, developer, fuser agent, staples, paper, g

insurance_bonds.text: EMENT OF OBJECTIVES (SOO) For Secure by-Design Space Vehicle (SDSV) Topic Area 3 1.0 Purpose The objective of this effort is to address cyber threats to national critical space missions (e.g., Position, Navigation, and Timing (PNT), Missile Warning/Missile Tracking (MW/MT), Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance (ISR), and Satellite Communications (SATCOM)) through the research, design, development, testing, and demonstration of a comprehensive Secure by-Design Space Vehicle (SDSV) system. 2.0 Background Space vehicles are increasingly recognized as vulnerable platforms facing sophisticated cyber threats. To ensure mission assurance, there is a critical need to provide advanced defensive solutions for space assets. This project aims to reduce the attack surfaces of space vehicles and implement robust resiliency mechanisms that enable self-protection and rapid recovery from cyber anomalies, leveraging Cyber-Hardened Satellite Software (CHSS) technology. 3.0 Period and Place of Performance • Period of Performance: The anticipated period of performance is a 12-month Base effort, followed by three (3) 12-month Option periods, plus 3 months for final reporting (Total 51 Months). • Place of Performance: The work will be performed primarily at the contractors facilit

To ensure mission assurance, there is a critical need to provide advanced defensive solutions for space assets. The Government has provided a Draft Statement of Objectives (SOO) Data Exchange Platform Operations, Modernization, and Development as Attachment 1 to this AOI. Attachment 1, Draft SOO establishes the Government’s technical and performance objectives. Vendors must use it as the baseline for their proposed technical solution and draft performance-based work statement. 2.0 Problem Statements & Desired Outcomes 2.1 Problem Statement The EIDS PMO must sustain mission-essential legacy data-exchange services while modernizing those services without degrading operational availability, cybersecurity, data integrity, or interoperability with mission partners. The current environment includes legacy Data Exchange Services (DES), Clinical Health Data Repository (CHDR), and Access Control Services Data Access Layer (ACS-DAL) capabilities requiring continuous operations, monitoring, maintenance, incident response, security compliance, and interface management. At the same time, the Government must transition legacy SOAP-based data exchanges toward cloud-native, containerized, RESTful, standards-based services that support near-real-time data exchange and future AI/ML use cases. 2.2 Desired Outcomes and Technical Focus Areas

elligent Automation and Partner Enablement The Government seeks to prepare the DxP for responsible downstream AI/ML applications and to reduce the time and effort required to onboard authorized mission partners. Responses must address the vendor’s approach to building automated ML data- preparation pipelines, supporting low-latency clinical inference use cases, creating a self-service developer portal, and providing automated onboarding workﬂows and sandboxes to accelerate partner integration. 2.3 Crosscutting Desired Outcomes Across all focus areas, the Government seeks a solution that: 1. Sustains mission-essential operations and cybersecurity while modernization is underway. 2. Delivers measurable performance, availability, incident-response, vulnerability- remediation, and engineering-quality outcomes consistent with Attachment 1, Draft SOO. 3. Uses transparent delivery and dependency-management practices, including Government Azure DevOps (ADO), where provided. 4. Produces current, usable technical documentation and supports orderly transition- in, knowledge transfer, and transition-out. 5.
